papers.title_en: Generative models for simulation based filtering: Formulations and Empirical Comparisons
papers.authors: Mohammad Al-Jarrah, Wei Deng, Bamdad Hosseini, Amirhossein Taghvaei
papers.evidence: 通过前向-后向随机微分方程实现薛定谔桥用于滤波
papers.tldr: 非线性滤波中，生成模型正成为后验采样与分布传输的新工具。本文给出统一框架，把分析步视为预报分布到后验的传输，并据此推导基于随机插值、确定性流匹配极限及前向-后向SDE薛定谔桥的三个新滤波器，同时提出分离训练与在线微调的两阶段调参流程。在受控实验中，这些生成滤波均能刻画EnKF和SIR难以处理的多峰后验，但不存在绝对最优框架，方法选择取决于在线预算与集合大小，且粒子轨迹正则性存在差异。
papers.abstract_en: This letter presents a unified formulation and a controlled numerical comparison of generative-model approaches to the nonlinear filtering problem. Under this formulation the analysis step is realized by a transport of the forecast distribution to the posterior, the approaches differing only in how that transport is selected and learned. We derive three new filters, based on stochastic interpolants, their deterministic flow-matching limit, and Schrödinger bridges realized through forward--backward SDEs. We develop a two-stage tuning procedure that separates the training of the generative model from its online refinement. The resulting methods are compared against the optimal transport filter (OTF), the Knothe--Rosenblatt filter (KRF), the sequential importance resampling (SIR) particle filter and the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), in terms of accuracy, computational time, and sensitivity to ensemble size and state dimension. The results indicate that every generative filter resolves multimodal posteriors that the EnKF and SIR do not, that no single generative framework dominates, the preferred method being set by the available online budget and ensemble size, and that the filters differ in the regularity of the particle trajectories they produce.

papers.title_en: Stable Filters for Generative Modeling of Graph Signals
papers.evidence: 图感知薛定谔桥生成模型的稳定性
papers.tldr: 图信号生成需要置换等变且对图结构扰动稳定的模型，但图感知薛定谔桥中拓扑扰动如何传播并影响生成分布尚不明确。本文分析漂移由图滤波器与图神经网络组成的连续时间生成模型，推导相对图扰动的Wasserstein稳定性界。基于该界提出稳定图滤波器设计框架，在保留图热扩散平滑性的同时增强结构稳定性。合成与fMRI实验表明，该方法提升结构鲁棒性，生成质量匹配或超越热方程基线。
papers.abstract_en: Generating signals on graphs requires permutation-equivariant models that exhibit stability with respect to relative structural perturbations. While recent graph-aware Schrödinger bridge models incorporate topology information directly into their reference dynamics, it is unclear how perturbations of the graph propagate through these dynamics and affect the resulting generated distributions. In this paper, we analyze the structural stability of graph-aware continuous-time generative models whose drift combines a graph filter with a learned graph neural network. We derive explicit Wasserstein stability bounds that quantify the effect of relative graph perturbations on the generated distributions. Motivated by these bounds, we introduce a principled framework for designing stable graph filters that preserve the smoothing behavior of graph heat diffusion, while boosting structural stability. Experiments on synthetic and fMRI signals show our stable filters enhance structural robustness while matching or exceeding the generative quality of the heat equation baseline.
